findings: Integration testing gap — Unit tests mock all external dependencies (database connections, subprocess execution, file I/O). No integration test evidence exists in .agents/evidence/runs/ showing the workflow executed against a real test database. Add integration tests that spin up an actual PostgreSQL container, run the full verification pipeline, and verify cleanup.

Hardcoded database allowlists — TRUSTED_TEST_HOSTS and TRUSTED_TEST_DATABASES are frozen sets defined in safety.py source code. Adding a new test environment requires code modification and redeployment. Move allowlists to configuration (environment variables or config file) with fallback to safe defaults.

Cleanup verification uses docker-compose ps output parsing — verify_database_dropped() checks if 'up' and 'test-postgres' appear in docker-compose ps stdout. This is brittle if docker-compose output format changes or if the string matching isn't precise enough. Use structured output (docker-compose ps --format json) or docker inspect API for more reliable verification.

No evidence of workflow execution in .agents/evidence/runs/ — The review scope includes 'integration test results in .agents/evidence/runs/' but no files exist in that directory. This confirms unit tests pass but provides no evidence the workflow runs successfully end-to-end.

FEAT status shows 'completed' but no execution evidence — All five FEAT files report status 'completed' with findings describing unit test results. None mention integration test execution or end-to-end workflow verification, reinforcing the gap between unit-level correctness and system-level safety.

Publisher depends on git ls-remote for SHA verification — fetch_remote_sha() parses git ls-remote origin HEAD output to get the remote SHA. This assumes the remote URL is trusted and hasn't been tampered with. If an attacker compromises the .git/config remote URL, the SHA comparison would validate against the wrong remote. Consider adding remote URL verification or using signed commits for publication verification.
